findings.description: Native large count_tokens can be gzip compressed; gateway sends identical decoded JSON uncompressed because restore is gated by messages billing and path.

Native gzip block mode 2 supplies Content-Encoding as an application header; serializer always places it after application headers. Bytes/values match, order differs in all 8 block-mode transport combinations.

Content-Encoding is absent from the wire-casing map; lowercase account overrides are missed and may coexist with a generated canonical key. Identity override yielded 8 gzip/200 and 4 identity/400 results across 12 actual sends; mapped body plus gzip override yielded 2 BadGzipFile/400 results.

experiment_notes: Initial combined audit lacked testdata mount for the policy test; forwarding and generic outputs completed, policy test was rerun separately with the correct fixtures.

The first policy observation used the same case-limited getter as production and missed lowercase values. Final observations record all case variants and export actual request bytes for independent transport validation.

One initial threaded HTTPS-proxy run ended with a TLS decoding error. The source of that isolated failure was not separately assigned; a separate relay with single-thread SSL I/O completed all 32 combinations. Original failure evidence was retained.
Block mode 1 on an empty cache used runtime compression; this round does not establish multi-turn block reuse.
Traced transport probe only initializes the production recorder in its main wrapper; production transport implementations are unchanged. This is not full deployed gateway authentication validation.
